{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABiJJPTA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhLg5BY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 235, "title": "Remove bundled demos and redundant media insertion UI; capture the mouse with Pointer Lock on click", "body": "## Goal

Follow up on the screen-first redesign in #233. Simplify the browser player further by **permanently removing the two bundled demo programs and their launcher, removing the redundant automatic-insertion button, and replacing the opt-in mouse checkbox with automatic click-to-capture Pointer Lock**.

The maintainer explicitly does **not** want backward compatibility, deprecated aliases, dormant code, feature flags, or provisions for restoring the removed features later. Delete their active implementation and assets completely instead of hiding them. This is a normal forward deletion from the repository/build; do not rewrite published Git history or historical Issue/PR records.

## 1. Remove both bundled demo programs completely

Current [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) exposes a Demos button (`#demos`), a `#demo-picker` popover, and two choices: Star Trail (`#game`) and Hello world + BEEP (`#hello`). These are no longer wanted. The normal application already boots FreeDOS on Ap and accepts users' own disk images.

- Delete both demo programs' source, binaries/disk images, generated files and demo-specific build/packaging/fetch paths from the current tracked tree and public distribution. Inspect `fixtures/hello98/`, `tools/build_media.py`, `web/media/`, Rust demo-generation code, package/build scripts, publication manifests/allowlists, and any Star Trail or hello98 references to identify every exclusively demo-related artifact. Do not leave private/demo-only copies in a new directory, a hidden picker or a dormant endpoint.
- Delete Demos, its entire popover, handlers, launch/reset helpers used exclusively by the demos, CSS, dedicated DOM IDs/state, demo media provenance/credits/licenses that apply exclusively to removed assets, and current documentation/help/README/usage references. Retain the project license and every notice required for remaining distributed content.
- Delete demo-specific tests and expectations. Where a removed demo was used as a vehicle for an independent CPU/device/audio/media/browser regression, replace it with a small original purpose-built test-only fixture or another existing rights-cleared non-demo fixture. Do not keep either removed program merely to satisfy an old test. Preserve substantive regression coverage, not compatibility with obsolete demo selectors or binaries.
- Preserve the bundled FreeDOS HDD, genuine test-only fixtures (e.g. ADV98, FM/PCM, floppy/device tests), generic disk boot/import paths and the emulator's ability to run user-supplied games. Those are not the two demo programs.

## 2. Remove the redundant Insert media button

The three explicit slots (IDE HDD, Floppy 1 and Floppy 2) already have Insert/Change actions. Delete the separate automatic-insertion button `#drive-auto` and its button-only UI, handlers and picker state. Do not replace it with another general-purpose insert button or a deprecated alias. Remove the now-empty `.media-actions` region and styles if unused.

- The per-drive Insert/Change popover remains the only visible file-selection entry point. Keep its Choose local file, Eject and Export actions, scoped to the selected drive. A disk-specific picker may retain a descriptive insertion heading; the removed item is the redundant standalone automatic-routing button.
- **Keep drag and drop**: dropping on the screen may continue to auto-route HDI/NHD to IDE HDD and supported floppy formats to FDD1, while dropping on an explicit slot uses that slot. This is the retained convenience agreed in the UI discussion, not a reason to retain the deleted button, its picker entry point or a compatibility shim. Retain only shared routing logic genuinely used by these supported flows.
- Rewrite file-format mismatch errors and Help to direct users to the correct existing drive, rather than a removed button. Remove old selector/API/test assumptions specific to the general auto-insert button.
- Keep dirty HDD discard confirmation, export-before-replace recovery, FreeDOS restoration, explicit boot source, profile restrictions, bounded chunked HDI/NHD I/O and local-only media behavior. Canceling a file chooser or destructive confirmation must preserve the existing disk and machine. Floppy insertion must not reset the guest.

## 3. Replace mouse opt-in with automatic click-to-capture Pointer Lock

Current [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js) gates pointer events on the `#mouse` checkbox and computes relative movement from bounded client coordinates; [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) exposes “Send mouse input to Ap guest” in Settings. The host and guest cursors can both appear and movement is limited by the screen edge. The desired experience is that of a normal desktop emulator.

### Required interaction

- Remove the `#mouse` checkbox, `#mouse-setting`, checkbox-specific state/event handlers, obsolete UI text and styles. No user preference or extra enable step is required.
- For a running PC-9821Ap guest, an intentional primary mouse click directly on the actual emulated canvas should **request Pointer Lock from that user gesture**, focus the screen and hide the host cursor while locked. Use the existing raw canvas as the input surface even when the CRT overlay is visible. Never request on page load, hover, arbitrary toolbar click or focus alone.
- The acquisition click is **capture-only**: suppress its press and release so it does not advance dialogue or activate a game button. Forward subsequent relative motion and supported mouse buttons to the guest only while capture is active. Use `movementX/Y` for locked relative movement instead of client-coordinate differences, with an appropriate consistent sensitivity and fractional accumulation where needed. Handle large movement without silently dropping distance at the existing signed-delta limit; bound/coalesce messages and retain ordering of press/release events. Preserve the bus mouse protocol and existing button mapping; do not implement an unrelated DOS mouse driver.
- Use `pointerlockchange` and `pointerlockerror` as authoritative state; support the browser API's synchronous/promise variations. On Escape the browser releases the pointer, restores the host cursor and stops sending mouse motion/buttons. Do not automatically recapture; another deliberate canvas click is required. Do not forward the host's unlock gesture as an accidental guest Escape; preserve normal guest Escape input when unlocked and provide the existing virtual key path if needed. Integrate with the existing F12 keyboard-capture/return-to-controls convention, without trapping keyboard-only users.
- On lock loss, pending lock failure, blur, visibility change, pause, reset, machine/profile change, fullscreen exit, Worker fault, or opening a host control that requires pointer access, release capture as appropriate, clear movement state and release any guest-held mouse buttons/keys at the existing safe boundary. Ensure a late lock resolution cannot capture a newly paused/replaced/unsupported machine. Preserve focus, menu operation and re-acquisition after a fresh click.
- PC-9801VM does not expose Ap bus mouse: do not request lock for that profile. Guest mouse functionality still depends on supported guest software/DOS driver, but the host capture interaction must not require knowing this in advance.
- On touch devices, browsers lacking Pointer Lock, or rejected requests, provide an automatic bounded pointer/touch fallback on the canvas where supported (no resurrected enable checkbox, no persistent global capture). Do not pretend the pointer is locked or leave it hidden after failure. Retain practical touch access and page navigation outside the screen. A concise recoverable status/Help note is sufficient; avoid a persistent intrusive overlay.
- Add minimal Help text such as “Click the screen to capture the mouse; press Esc to release.” Explain the Ap mouse-driver limitation and fallback only as needed. Keep the normal player uncluttered.

## Implementation boundaries

Inspect `web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/style.css`, relevant tests and documentation, packaging/build scripts and fixtures. Reuse current guest mouse RPC, keyboard focus and media transaction handling. No changes to guest CPU clocks, JIT, IRQ timing, disk format support, CRT defaults, raw screenshots, stereo sound, rendering architecture or existing performance optimizations unless a narrowly necessary input fix is independently justified.

Do not preserve dead code, compatibility routes, old IDs/aliases, unused assets or commented-out implementations for the removed features. Search the current tree and inspect the built site to confirm cleanup; historical commits and historical issue records need not be rewritten.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] No Demos button/picker, Star Trail or Hello world + BEEP program/source/image, or exclusively demo-specific build path, current documentation, test, or public asset remains. No replacement bundled demo feature. Independent core regressions previously using the demos are migrated to non-demo fixtures without weakening coverage.
- [ ] No standalone Insert media auto-insertion button or compatibility alias remains. Each drive's picker still works, screen/slot drag-and-drop routes correctly, mismatched formats show useful errors, and cancel/dirty-HDD/export/restore/boot behavior is preserved.
- [ ] No mouse-enable checkbox or checkbox state remains. On a real browser with Pointer Lock available, clicking the running Ap canvas (raw and CRT) captures the pointer and does not send the acquisition click to the guest; subsequent relative motion and left/right press/release reach the actual Wasm guest, including movement beyond screen boundaries. Escape reliably releases it, prevents stray guest input and allows host UI use; a subsequent click reacquires.
- [ ] Exercise pause/reset/profile switch, fullscreen enter/exit, focus loss, visibility, capture failure/race and held buttons; no stuck input, surprise reacquisition or host pointer remaining hidden. VM never locks; touch/unsupported fallback stays usable. Check keyboard-only access, guest keys/F12, popovers and visible focus.
- [ ] Verify normal FreeDOS auto-boot, existing per-drive media flows, CRT modes/default, audio/stereo and responsive layout remain functional. Update the browser tests to exercise the actual new flows, including genuine browser Pointer Lock integration plus targeted deterministic state/error tests where native browser restrictions require them. Do not rely solely on mocked success or waive existing substantive regressions.
- [ ] Run applicable native/release-Wasm, browser, audio, packaging/security/license tests and build at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Verify the publication asset audit no longer includes the removed demo media. Record limitations honestly; no proprietary game files/captures in Git.

Related: #233 (UI redesign), #120/#130 (media routing and FreeDOS boot), #191/#195 (CRT), #146 (game playback). This issue intentionally supersedes the previous UI redesign requirement to keep both bundled demo launchers and a visible general auto-insert entry point.

## Required post-merge verification
